papers.what_it_is: Introduces a quantum data embedding by ground state preparation of a parameterized Hamiltonian and analyzes its frequency spectrum.

assertions.value: The authors report that ground state-based feature maps can be seen as models whose frequency gap spectrum grows at least as a high-degree polynomial in the number of qubits N, and becomes exponential for complex Hamiltonians.
quotes: ground state-based feature maps can be seen as models with large capacity, where the frequency gap spectrum grows at least as a high-degree polynomial in the number of qubits N
For complex Hamiltonians this scaling of the degree and size of the spectrum becomes exponential.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical result of this paper, not a numbered theorem.

assertions.value: The authors report that the spectrum is largely degenerate and its coefficients are highly structured, which they say gives models of limited expressivity.
quotes: We observed that the spectrum is largely degenerate, and frequencies are tied with coefficients for the emerging basis that are highly structured.
This leads to highly specific models with limited expressivity, where formally large model capacity is effectively tamed.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical result of this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that they analyze the feature map by recasting it as an adiabatic state preparation procedure with Trotterized evolution, and give an alternative analysis in an appendix to show the conclusion does not depend on that choice.
quotes: We analyze the corresponding quantum feature map, recasting it as an adiabatic state preparation procedure with Trotterized evolution.
We show that this is not the case by presenting in the Appendix an alternative analysis
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own analysis setup in the abstract and Section IV.

papers.title_in_file: Higher-Order Portfolio Optimization with Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
papers.what_it_is: Formulates portfolio optimization with skewness and kurtosis as a HUBO problem and tests QAOA on 100 simulated instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that an experimental evaluation of 100 portfolio optimization problems shows the HUBO formulation solutions often correspond to better portfolio allocations than the classical baseline.
quotes: Our extensive experimental evaluation of 100 portfolio optimization problems shows that the solutions to the HUBO formulation often correspond to better portfolio allocations than the classical baseline.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract does not say whether the solutions are the exact HUBO optimum or the QAOA output; the results table was not read cell by cell.

assertions.value: The authors report that the 100 random problems were chosen to fit a 15-qubit simulator.
quotes: This way, we obtained 100 random portfolio optimization problems that were ensured to fit a 15qubit simulator.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states how its dataset was built.

assertions.value: The authors state that the resource requirements for solving HUBO problems with QAOA are likely too demanding for current hardware.
quotes: While the resource requirements for solving HUBO problems with QAOA are likely too demanding for the current hardware
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VI states the limit.

assertions.value: The authors report an average QAOA enhancement factor of 14.43, meaning the minimizing state is on average 14.43x more probable to be measured than under a random state.
quotes: The average enhancement across all cases is 14.43, which means that on average it is 14.43x more probable to measure the minimizing state compared to a random state.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulation.

papers.title_in_file: SPHERICAL AND HYPERBOLIC TORIC TOPOLOGY-BASED CODES ON GRAPH EMBEDDING FOR ISING MRF MODELS: CLASSICAL AND QUANTUM TOPOLOGY MACHINE LEARNING
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Sections 5.2 and 6, Table 1; the 60-page body of theory was skimmed, not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: An early-draft preprint relating LDPC codes on graphs to Ising models, DNN architectures and QAOA.

assertions.value: The authors state that QAOA on the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Ising model can be considered analogous to the back-propagation loss landscape in DNN training, and that QAOA layer depth p correlates to the number of belief propagation decoding iterations.
quotes: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) utilized in the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Ising model can be considered analogous to back-propagation loss function landscape in training DNN.
Furthermore, the layer depth (p) in QAOA correlates to the number of decoding BP iterations in the Wiberg (covering) decoding tree.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract statement; the abstract gives no evidence for it.

assertions.value: The authors report that their code-on-graph construction methods outperform the Chord Protocol-based factorization method across the majority of datasets.
quotes: outperforming the Chord Protocol-based factorization method previously employed in the superior transformer architecture, ChordMixed, across the majority of datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison in one study (Table 1 of approximation errors, classical matrices).

assertions.value: The paper labels itself an early draft preprint.
quotes: AN EARLY DRAFT PREPRINT
assertions.certainty_reason: Title page states its own status.

papers.title_in_file: Automatic Structural Search of Tensor Network States including Entanglement Renormalization
papers.what_it_is: An algorithm that searches tensor network structures, including entanglement renormalization, by local rearrangement guided by variational energy.

assertions.value: The authors report that their algorithm for the spin-1/2 tetramer singlets model could calculate the exact ground energy starting from a MERA structure.
quotes: Firstly, we demonstrated that our algorithm for the spin-1/2 tetramer singlets model could calculate exact ground energy using the multi-scale entanglement renormalization ansatz (MERA) structure as an initial TN structure.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one small model.

assertions.value: The authors report that on random XY models, from both initial structures, the algorithm improves variational energy, fidelity and entanglement entropy, with larger improvement from the structure based on the strong disordered renormalization group.
quotes: We found that, in both cases, our algorithm achieves improvements in variational energy, fidelity, and entanglement entropy.
The degree of improvement in these quantities is superior in the latter case compared to the former
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on 1D random XY models.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithm does not converge to the exact target state in the tetramer model when it keeps adopting the minimum-energy structure, and that larger bond dimension and larger systems are needed to extend its applicability.
quotes: we encountered a problem where our algorithm does not converge to the exact target state when continually adopting the structure with minimum variational energy.
Expanding the bond dimension and applying it to larger systems are essential steps to enhance the applicability of our method.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section V states these limits.

papers.title_in_file: A Quantum Natural Language Processing Approach to Pronoun Resolution
papers.what_it_is: Gives quantum circuit semantics for discourse relations via truncated Fock spaces and tests them in simulation on a pronoun resolution task.

assertions.value: The authors report that the highest accuracies were recorded for models with a notion of discourse, where the anaphora was resolved, regardless of grammatical structure.
quotes: The highest accuracies were recorded for models with a notion of discourse (i.e. the anaphora was resolved), irregardless of presence of a grammatical structure.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on a small dataset in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that combining the sentences of each discourse with a CNOT (Frobenius multiplication) achieved higher accuracy than a controlled-RZ rotation.
quotes: revealed that the CNOT combination (Frobenius multiplication) achieves a higher accuracy than a controlled- RZ rotation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on a small dataset in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiments ran on IBMQ AerSimulations of the circuits for a definite pronoun resolution task, and that the dataset is small, with a larger dataset in progress.
quotes: We then experiment with the IBMQ AerSimulations of these circuits in a definite pronoun resolution task
Most important of these is that our dataset is small; experimentation on a larger dataset is work in progress.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 7 states the dataset limit; the abstract states the setup.

papers.title_in_file: Dual variational quantum eigensolver: A quantum algorithm to lower bound the ground-state energy
papers.version_note: File is arXiv v3 dated March 2026 although stored under 2023; title and content match the record.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes dual-VQE, a variational algorithm giving a lower-bound estimate of a Hamiltonian ground-state energy.

assertions.value: The authors propose dual-VQE, which produces a lower-bound estimate of the ground-state energy, complementing the upper bound from VQE.
quotes: Here we propose a dual variational quantum eigensolver (dual-VQE) that produces a lower-bound estimate of the ground-state energy.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its own algorithm in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that Theorem 1 guarantees a rigorous lower bound only in a limit of the penalty parameter c, and that for finite c the value is technically an estimate rather than a strict bound.
quotes: While Theorem 1 guarantees that dual-VQE provides a rigorous lower bound on the ground-state energy in the limit
for finite c, the value provided by dual-VQE is technically an estimate rather than a strict bound.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section V, citing Theorem 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that with a convex combination ansatz and a classical generative model, the quantum resources to evaluate the dual-VQE objective are no greater than those for VQE.
quotes: When using a convex combination ansatz in conjunction with a classical generative model, the quantum computational resources needed to evaluate the objective function of dual-VQE are no greater than those needed for that of VQE.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytical claim in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report simulations on the transverse-field Ising model in which dual-VQE training is slower and noisier than VQE, yet approaches the true value.
quotes: while dual-VQE training is slower and noisier than VQE, it approaches the true value
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one example.

papers.title_in_file: Scalable Quantum Neural Networks for Classification
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a scalable QNN that splits features across several small quantum devices, tested in simulation on binary MNIST.

assertions.value: The authors report that the SQNN model achieves comparable classification accuracy to a regular QNN of the same scale and that more quantum resources significantly improve SQNN accuracy.
quotes: It shows that the SQNN model achieves a comparable classification accuracy to a regular QNN model of the same scale.
Furthermore, it demonstrates that the SQNN model with more quantum resources can significantly improve classification accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result in simulation on one binary task.

assertions.value: The authors report that among regular QNN classifiers with three blocks, the 16qb 3blk model with 16 data qubits had the best validation accuracy of 92.04%.
quotes: Among the QNN classifiers with three blocks, 16qb 3blk model with 16 data qubits has the best accuracy of 92.04% on the validation dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work is exploratory, run on a classical simulator with TensorFlow Quantum on binary MNIST, and that the simulator limits circuits to at most 17 qubits.
quotes: Our work is exploratory and carried out on a quantum system simulator using the TensorFlow Quantum library.
a VQC made up of basic quantum blocks can only contain at most 17 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its setup and simulator limit.

papers.title_in_file: Big data applications on small quantum computers
papers.what_it_is: Applies coresets with VQE to divisive, 3-means and Gaussian mixture clustering Hamiltonians on small quantum computers.

assertions.value: The authors report noiseless simulations of up to 25 qubits on CUDA Quantum in which the approach provides comparable performance to classical solvers.
quotes: We perform noiseless simulations on instances of sizes up to 25 qubits on CUDA Quantum and show that our approach provides comparable performance to classical solvers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from noiseless simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that divisive clustering and Gaussian mixture modeling need a number of qubits equal to the coreset size, while their 3-means Hamiltonian needs twice the coreset size.
quotes: We show that the number of qubits required to perform divisive clustering and Gaussian mixture modeling in a quantum computer is equal to the size of the coreset.
On the other hand, we derive a Hamiltonian that requires a number of qubits that is twice the size of the coreset to perform 3-mean clustering
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived by the authors in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that errors were not a concern in their simulations but are a concern on hardware, and that the two-label 3-means representation forces a coreset of half the size for a given qubit count.
quotes: We do not need to worry about errors in computation for our simulations, however, we highlight this issue as it becomes a concern when implementing algorithms on quantum hardware.
the two-label representation effectively forces us to use a coreset of half the size that we could have used
assertions.certainty_reason: Section V states these limits.
